title: Are AI recommendations equally achievable?
summary: Auditing the cost and availability of algorithmic recourse across groups.
overview: A model may offer a route to a different prediction while making that route harder for some groups. This project studies that question on the IBM HR attrition dataset.
constraints: Counterfactual changes were constrained by immutable features and salary-change caps. The chosen cost definition affects the interpretation of fairness.
contribution: My documented role was fairness and FACTS analysis, results and visualization. Preprocessing, predictive models and the DiCE pipeline were shared team work.
approach: We compared Random Forest and XGBoost through prediction, feature-change sensitivity and recourse metrics. The analysis examines effectiveness, cost and access within a fixed budget.
results: The notebook contains saved tables and plots comparing subgroups. A salary-cap sensitivity analysis explores how results change under tighter constraints. The figure below is an original project output.
limits: This is an academic audit, not a deployed HR system. Feature-flip sensitivity is not causal validation; conclusions depend on the data, cost model and subgroup sample sizes.
